Keystone

An information system for the life cycle of a dwelling: an inventory of building components with service lives and replacement costs, a ten-year capital plan, preventive maintenance, structured diagnosis and a platform for the contractors who carry out the work, with the illustrated book Inside Your House.

Visit the site ↗How to useEngineering record

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Designed and shipped a local-first application for owners and contractors, with its sync engine, the Postgres security model and the companion book. The hard part was letting two parties act on the same job without giving either one write access to the other’s data.

System architecture

Device
  • React app: Home, Pro, Parts
  • Dexie tables in IndexedDB
diff by hash
Server
  • Sync engine (push own rows, pull visible rows)
  • RPC: accept_quote, complete_job
SQL + RLS
Data
  • Supabase Postgres, RLS per household
  • private schema helpers

The app always reads and writes Dexie, so it works offline exactly as in the demo. Every 15 seconds the sync engine compares each row with the hash of its last synced version, pushes only rows the user owns, and pulls whatever the server’s policies let the user see. Actions that touch both sides, such as accepting a quote, call security definer functions that check ownership and write both records in one transaction.

Key engineering decisions

01

Local-first, cloud as replica

The same code path serves the offline demo and signed-in accounts; the network only adds sync. A visit without signal is never blocked.

02

Ownership rules in two places

The client only pushes rows it owns and the server’s RLS enforces the same rule, so a modified client still cannot write someone else’s home.

03

Two-party actions on the server

Accepting a quote or closing a job writes to both owner and contractor records, so it runs as a checked function in one transaction instead of two client writes.

Notes for reviewers

Data modelHomes, systems, records, documents, tasks, reserves, inventory, contacts; on the contractor side businesses, requests, quotes, jobs, invoices and reviews.
Limits and next stepsSync is interval-based with last-write-wins per row; the next step is Realtime subscriptions and field-level merge for shared records, then finishing Keystone Parts.
01

Problem statement

Most owners learn how their house works only when something fails. Component ages are printed on labels no one reads, warranties disappear into email, and major replacements (roof, furnace, air conditioning) tend to fall within a few years of each other with no reserve set aside. Contractors keep their own notes, so the history of the building is scattered across every job.

02

Contribution

Keystone Home records each system and component with its installation year and life stage, derives a replacement year and aggregates these into a ten-year capital plan adjusted for inflation, with a monthly savings target and a preparedness score. The same inventory generates the maintenance calendar. A fifteen-question Home Health Snapshot returns a score out of 100 and corrective tasks. Diagnose treats 36 common faults as decision procedures that open with a safety question and end, where needed, in a request to professionals serving the ZIP code. Keystone Pro provides those professionals with leads, quotes, scheduling, job records with before-and-after photographs, estimates and invoices; a completed job is written back into the owner’s history. Owners can export a home history report, an insurance loss packet and a transfer file for a buyer.

03

Architecture

One React and TypeScript application serves the owner, contractor, parts and book surfaces. Each account keeps a local copy of its data and synchronises with Supabase every 15 seconds, so the application remains usable offline. Row-level security isolates each household, and operations that involve both parties (accepting a quote, closing a job, settling an invoice) run on the server.

04

Method and data

Service lives and costs are national planning estimates, not measurements of a particular building. The parts finder resolves a part by model number, part number or symptom and links to Amazon with an Associates tag; no Amazon price or image is shown. Every chapter of the book links to the corresponding screen of the application.

05

Verification and limitations

Contractors cannot pay for ranking, which keeps the order of referrals independent of revenue. Cost projections carry the uncertainty of national averages and should be read as planning ranges. Keystone Parts is not yet complete.
